title: Connecting Stellar Population Surveys to Stellar Evolution with Delay-time Distributions: Application to LMC Classical Cepheids
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: The progenitors of many stellar-origin phenomena such as supernovae, evolved giants and supergiants, planetary nebulae, AGB stars and other post-main-sequence exotica remain poorly understood due to stellar evolution uncertainties such as mass-loss, binary evolution, rotation, mixing, and overshooting. A promising technique for investigating stellar progenitor scenarios with resolved stellar population surveys of galaxies is the delay-time distribution (DTD). Given a survey of stellar phenomena of interest, the DTD extracts the progenitor age distribution and production rates of the phenomena from star-formation history (SFH) maps of galaxies. Here we test the potential of DTDs as a stellar evolution diagnostic by applying to stars with known ages -- Classical Cepheids in the LMC. We use the high-completeness OGLE-IV survey of Cepheids, and LMC SFH maps from optical and near-infrared surveys. The measured DTDs from optical SFH maps show significant detections at ages of 20-200 Myr for FU Cepheids, and 125-200 Myr for FO Cepheids. These are consistent with independently measured ages from the period-age-color relations, with the DTD peak being more consistent with relations from non-canonical models that include effects of overshooting, rotational mixing etc. An outlier population of 0.5-0.8 Gyr of FU Cepheids is also detected in the DTD, though its veracity is debatable given the brightness and pulsation periods of FU Cepheids, and because the signal is not recovered with DTDs derived from near-infrared SFH. For upcoming surveys (e.g. with Roman), DTDs of stars with well-constrained progenitors such as Cepheids and RR Lyrae can provide independent verification of the derived SFHs.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the delay-time distribution (DTD) technique as a stellar evolution diagnostic using Classical Cepheids in the LMC from OGLE-IV and SFH maps. DTDs from optical SFH detect FU Cepheids at 20-200 Myr and FO Cepheids at 125-200 Myr, consistent with non-canonical models including overshooting and rotation. A debated older FU Cepheid population (0.5-0.8 Gyr) is also found. DTDs can verify SFHs in future surveys like Roman.
AI.motivation: Progenitors of many stellar-origin phenomena (supernovae, giants, planetary nebulae, AGB stars) are poorly understood due to stellar evolution uncertainties like mass-loss, binary evolution, rotation, mixing, and overshooting. The DTD is a promising technique to derive progenitor age distributions and production rates from SFH maps of galaxies.
AI.method: The DTD technique was applied to Classical Cepheids (with known ages) in the LMC using the high-completeness OGLE-IV survey and SFH maps from optical and near-infrared surveys. Measured DTDs were compared to independently measured ages from period-age-color relations, including both canonical and non-canonical stellar models.
AI.result: Optical SFH maps yield DTD detections at 20-200 Myr for FU Cepheids and 125-200 Myr for FO Cepheids. The DTD peak better matches non-canonical models (overshooting, rotational mixing). An outlier FU Cepheid population at 0.5-0.8 Gyr was detected in optical but not recovered in near-infrared DTDs, making its veracity debatable.
AI.conclusion: DTDs are a valid stellar evolution diagnostic, confirmed by independent age measurements. For upcoming surveys (e.g., Roman), DTDs of stars with well-constrained progenitors (Cepheids, RR Lyrae) can provide independent verification of derived SFHs.

title: Modeling the curved dust sublimation front in protoplanetary disks: a potential probe of midplane turbulence
summary: We present a new approach to calculate the geometry and emission of the dust inner wall in disks around T Tauri stars. This calculation follows a self-consistent approach given the disk structure and adopts a density-dependent sublimation temperature for the dust. We built spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of disk models with curved walls around a $0.5\,M_\odot$ star, finding that the curved wall starts at a radius of $\sim 0.11$ au and extends to $\sim 0.38$ au. The dependence on mass accretion rate, dust settling, and disk inclination on the resulting SEDs is explored, as well as the impact of the height of the midplane layer containing large millimeter-sized grains. To test our models, we compare synthetic near-IR colors from a grid of disk models with observed colors for a large sample of disk-bearing T Tauri stars located in Taurus, IC 348, and the Orion complex. Most of the observed colors can be explained by combinations of mass accretion rates, dust settling, and inclinations within the expected ranges for T Tauri stars. However, populating the regions where observed JHK colors are most concentrated, requires the millimeter-size grains be spread up to 0.5--3 scale heights above the midplane. This result contradicts expectations of rapid dust settling and suggests a high degree of turbulence capable of lifting large grains toward the upper disk layers. These findings provide insight into the dynamical conditions of the disk midplane near the star.

AI.tldr: A self-consistent model of curved dust inner walls in T Tauri disks with density-dependent sublimation temperatures shows that reproducing observed near-IR colors requires millimeter-sized grains to be lofted 0.5–3 scale heights above the midplane, implying high turbulence contrary to expectations of rapid dust settling.
AI.motivation: To develop a self-consistent calculation of the geometry and emission of the dust inner wall in T Tauri disks that accounts for density-dependent sublimation temperatures, and to test this model against a large sample of observed near-IR colors across multiple star-forming regions.
AI.method: The authors built SEDs of disk models with curved inner walls around a 0.5 M☉ star, adopting a density-dependent sublimation temperature. They explored dependencies on mass accretion rate, dust settling, disk inclination, and the vertical distribution of millimeter-sized grains. Synthetic near-IR colors from a grid of models were compared with observed JHK colors of disk-bearing T Tauri stars in Taurus, IC 348, and Orion.
AI.result: Models with curved inner walls predict a sublimation radius from ~0.11 au extending to ~0.38 au. While most observed colors can be explained by combinations of accretion rate, settling, and inclination, the densest regions of observed JHK color space require millimeter-sized grains to be distributed up to 0.5–3 scale heights above the midplane.
AI.conclusion: The need for large grains at high altitudes contradicts rapid dust settling expectations and suggests a high degree of turbulence capable of lifting large grains toward the upper disk layers, providing insight into the dynamical conditions near the star-disk interface.

title: Prediction for IMAP: Revealing the Role of the Solar Magnetic Field in the Heliotail
comment: Submitted to ApJL
summary: The classic paradigm of the heliosphere considered the solar magnetic field as having a passive role in the heliosheath, yet recent work has suggested that the solar magnetic field plays an active role by collimating the solar wind plasma. Previous work has suggested that high-latitude lobes observed by IBEX-Hi energetic neutral atom (ENA) maps are solely due to the fast/slow solar wind profile, yet other works have found that the solar magnetic field may play a role in organizing the lobes as well. Here, using an MHD solution with and without the solar magnetic field, we find that the fast/slow wind profile largely dictates the ENA profile up to 10 keV. Beyond this energy, the collimation effects are more prominent and the fast/slow solar wind profile no longer organizes the maps. The collimation creates two high latitude lobes. At 80 keV, the split-tail heliosphere yields an enhancement of ENAs of the high-latitude tail lobes compared to the low-latitude region by a factor of $\sim$2, IMAP should be able to see whether the solar magnetic field collimates the solar wind, as well as probe the shape of the deep heliotail.

AI.tldr: The solar magnetic field actively collimates the solar wind in the heliosheath, creating two high-latitude lobes in ENA maps at energies above 10 keV, with a ~2x ENA enhancement in the high-latitude tail lobes at 80 keV compared to low-latitude regions.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the solar magnetic field plays an active role in collimating solar wind plasma in the heliosheath, beyond the previously assumed passive role and beyond the fast/slow solar wind profile effect on ENA maps.
AI.method: MHD simulations comparing solutions with and without the solar magnetic field, analyzing IBEX-Hi ENA maps across different energy ranges (up to 10 keV, and beyond).
AI.result: Below 10 keV, the fast/slow wind profile dominates ENA organization. Above 10 keV, collimation effects dominate, creating two high-latitude lobes. At 80 keV, the split-tail heliosphere shows ~2x ENA enhancement in high-latitude tail lobes relative to low-latitude regions.
AI.conclusion: IMAP should be capable of observing whether the solar magnetic field collimates the solar wind and probing the deep heliotail shape beyond the energy threshold where collimation effects become prominent.

title: Cepheids with giant companions III. Evolutionary modeling of nine binary double Cepheids from the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds
comment: 19 pages, 12 figures, accepted in Astronomy & astrophysics
summary: Binary double (BIND) Cepheids are systems comprising two Cepheid components. This feature provides important constraints that allow us to reveal the origin of Cepheids, trace their evolution, and test pulsation theory. Ten BIND Cepheids are now known, with only one having its parameters determined. We aim to estimate the physical parameters of the components of nine BIND Cepheids in the Magellanic Clouds and the Milky Way, investigate their evolutionary configurations, and formation scenarios. We also expand the parameter space of characterized individual Cepheids in mass, radius, period, and metallicity. We extended the recently introduced $q$-PED method to BIND Cepheids, combining observational constraints with theoretical pulsation and evolutionary models. We considered all consistent configurations (first-crossing, blue-loop, and mixed) as viable solutions. Probabilistic and observational constraints, including spectroscopic mass ratios for two systems, were then used to discriminate between them. We obtained new $q$-PED estimates of mass, radius, temperature, luminosity, and age for 18 Cepheids with previously unknown physical parameters. For one Galactic system, the spectroscopic mass ratio $q_s=0.84\pm0.04$ indicates a first-crossing plus a blue-loop Cepheid solution. This mass ratio, along with the predicted mass ratios lower than unity for two other systems, suggests past binary interactions and a likely merger origin for one component. We derive a new period--mass--radius relation and mass--luminosity relation covering the mass range $2.3-4.6$ M$_\odot$. This work provides the first mass estimates for Cepheids in the SMC, extending the lower Cepheid mass limit down to 2.3 M$_\odot$. Binary interactions in the past evolution of Cepheids may be common, affecting up to 40\% of our systems with two clear cases and two more if blue loop Cepheids are preferred.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the q-PED method to analyze nine BIND Cepheid systems, providing the first physical parameter estimates (mass, radius, temperature, luminosity, age) for 18 Cepheids, including the first mass estimates for SMC Cepheids (down to 2.3 M☉). The study finds evidence for past binary interactions in up to 40% of systems and derives new period-mass-radius and mass-luminosity relations.
AI.motivation: BIND Cepheids provide unique constraints to understand Cepheid origins, evolution, and pulsation theory. Only one of the ten known BIND Cepheids had determined parameters, leaving a significant gap in understanding these systems and their formation scenarios.
AI.method: Extended the q-PED method to BIND Cepheids by combining observational constraints with theoretical pulsation and evolutionary models. Considered three consistent configurations (first-crossing, blue-loop, mixed) and used probabilistic and observational constraints (including spectroscopic mass ratios for two systems) to discriminate between solutions.
AI.result: Obtained physical parameter estimates for 18 Cepheids with previously unknown parameters. Found a spectroscopic mass ratio q_s=0.84±0.04 for one Galactic system indicating first-crossing plus blue-loop solution. Derived new period-mass-radius and mass-luminosity relations across 2.3-4.6 M☉. Provided first mass estimates for SMC Cepheids, extending lower mass limit to 2.3 M☉. Evidence suggests binary interactions affect up to 40% of systems.
AI.conclusion: Binary interactions may be common in Cepheid evolution, affecting up to 40% of studied systems. The work significantly expands the parameter space of characterized Cepheids in mass, radius, period, and metallicity, and suggests past binary interactions and likely merger origins for some components.

title: Dark Matter in Draco and Boötes I: Hints of a Core in an Ultra-Faint Dwarf from Simulation-Based Inference
comment: 33 + 8 pages, 13 + 8 figures, 5 tables, submitted to MNRAS
summary: The density profiles of dwarf spheroidal galaxies are among the most sensitive probes of dark matter physics, yet extracting them from noisy stellar kinematics remains a fundamental obstacle. We present GraphNPE, a simulation-based inference method for dynamical mass modeling that incorporates measurement uncertainties and spectroscopic selection functions in the forward model. Using mock data, we show that methods relying solely on line-of-sight velocity dispersion are biased toward cuspy density profiles, even in the absence of the mass-anisotropy degeneracy. By accessing higher-order velocity moments, particularly line-of-sight kurtosis, GraphNPE breaks key degeneracies and recovers density profiles with substantially less bias. We apply GraphNPE to Draco and Boötes I using MMT/Hectochelle and DESI for Draco, and the S5 survey for Boötes I. For each, we report density profiles and dark matter $J$- and $D$-factors. For Draco, GraphNPE yields consistent results across datasets, marginally preferring a cuspy inner profile ($ρ_{150} \sim 1.6-1.9 \times 10^8\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{kpc}^{-3}$) in agreement with literature. On DESI, however, second-order Jeans modeling fits the dispersion but fails to reproduce the kurtosis, demonstrating higher-order moments are essential. For Boötes I, limited statistical power prevents definitive determination of the inner slope. GraphNPE recovers $ρ_{150} = 0.36^{+0.15}_{-0.11} \times 10^8\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{kpc}^{-3}$, significantly lower than literature and consistent with a cored inner profile. This places Boötes I among the lowest density dwarfs at comparable stellar masses.

AI.tldr: GraphNPE is a simulation-based inference method for dynamical mass modeling of dwarf spheroidal galaxies that uses higher-order velocity moments (esp. kurtosis) to break degeneracies and recover unbiased density profiles, demonstrated on Draco (marginally cuspy) and Boötes I (cored, low density).
AI.motivation: Extracting accurate density profiles of dwarf spheroidal galaxies from noisy stellar kinematics is fundamentally difficult; existing methods relying on line-of-sight velocity dispersion alone are biased toward cuspy profiles even without the mass-anisotropy degeneracy, motivating a new approach that incorporates measurement uncertainties and selection functions.
AI.method: GraphNPE: a simulation-based inference method that incorporates measurement uncertainties and spectroscopic selection functions in the forward model, and accesses higher-order velocity moments (particularly line-of-sight kurtosis) to break degeneracies in dynamical mass modeling.
AI.result: Using mock data, methods relying solely on velocity dispersion are biased toward cuspy profiles. For Draco, GraphNPE yields consistent results across datasets (MMT/Hectochelle, DESI) with ρ₁₅₀ ~ 1.6-1.9×10⁸ M⊙ kpc⁻³, marginally cuspy. For Boötes I (S5 survey), GraphNPE recovers ρ₁₅₀ = 0.36⁺⁰‧¹⁵₋₀‧₁₁ ×10⁸ M⊙ kpc⁻³, significantly lower than literature and consistent with a cored profile, placing it among the lowest density dwarfs at comparable stellar masses.
AI.conclusion: Higher-order velocity moments (kurtosis) are essential for unbiased density profile recovery; second-order Jeans modeling fails to reproduce observed kurtosis (e.g., on DESI Draco data), and GraphNPE effectively breaks degeneracies to recover density profiles with substantially less bias across different datasets and galaxies.

title: A Stellar Role Reversal: Multiple Features in the Mass and Mass Ratio Distributions of Merging Binary Black Holes from Stable Mass Transfer
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, to be submitted to AAS Journals, comments welcome
summary: Observations of gravitational wave events have enabled the measurement of the merging binary black hole (BBH) mass function. This mass function encodes the physical interactions which shape the formation and evolution of BBHs. In this work we investigate how the stable mass transfer (SMT) channel of BBH formation imprints onto the BBH primary mass and mass ratio distributions. We use both an analytic framework and binary population synthesis to show how assumptions about mass transfer accretion efficiency and mass transfer stability affect the BBH mass distribution. Under the assumption of conservative mass transfer, we find that the SMT channel produces two observationally distinct subpopulations: a high primary mass, near equal mass ratio population formed through mass ratio reversal (MRR), and a low primary mass non-MRR subpopulation. The mass range where MRR occurs is determined by assumptions about binary SMT. In particular, we find that the stability criteria for mass transfer at different stellar evolutionary stages carve out complementary regions in the primary-mass--mass-ratio plane, separating the MRR and non-MRR populations into distinct peaks at high and low primary mass respectively. Our results imply that the physics of SMT creates distinct features in gravitational wave populations which current and near future gravitational wave detectors may be able to resolve.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the stable mass transfer (SMT) channel of binary black hole formation imprints distinct features on the BBH primary mass and mass ratio distributions, showing that conservative mass transfer produces two subpopulations (mass ratio reversal and non-MRR) separated by stability criteria at different stellar evolutionary stages.
AI.motivation: To understand how the physics of stable mass transfer in binary black hole formation shapes the observable gravitational wave population, specifically how assumptions about mass transfer efficiency and stability affect the BBH mass function.
AI.method: Combined analytic framework and binary population synthesis to model the SMT channel of BBH formation, varying assumptions about mass transfer accretion efficiency and mass transfer stability criteria at different stellar evolutionary stages.
AI.result: Under conservative mass transfer, the SMT channel produces two distinct subpopulations: a high primary mass, near equal mass ratio population via mass ratio reversal (MRR), and a low primary mass non-MRR population. Stability criteria at different evolutionary stages create complementary regions separating these populations into distinct peaks.
AI.conclusion: The physics of SMT creates distinct features in gravitational wave populations that current and near-future gravitational wave detectors may be able to resolve.

title: Latent thermal instability
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. To be submitted, comments are welcome
summary: Multiscale temperature fluctuations are abundant in the intracluster medium (ICM) outside of galaxy cluster cores ($\sim 100~{\rm kpc}$). Their origin is often attributed to turbulent stirring by subhalos or accreting baryons crossing the virial radius. However, their apparent resistance to mixing and thermal conduction in a collisional medium has not been explained. We propose a new mechanism by which steady-state temperature fluctuations can form and persist outside the cluster core. Local thermal instability, or Field instability, is used to explain filamentary condensates in cluster cores but is usually dismissed outside them because thermal conduction should suppress instability. In weakly collisional or collisionless plasmas, however, thermal conduction can be anomalously suppressed by heat-flux-driven plasma instabilities triggered in presence of a local magnetic field, leading to two effects: (i) condensates form in a new parameter regime that overlaps with conditions outside the core, and (ii) condensates reach a steady state as in the hydrodynamic limit. This extends the regime of instability-driven fluctuations to over $\gtrsim50\%$ (depending on hot plasma temperature) of the cluster. We use one-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of condensates to test our analytical ideas.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that heat-flux-driven plasma instabilities can suppress thermal conduction in the intracluster medium (ICM) outside galaxy cluster cores, allowing local thermal instability (Field instability) to produce steady-state temperature fluctuations over a much larger fraction of clusters than previously thought.
AI.motivation: Multiscale temperature fluctuations are observed in the ICM outside cluster cores (~100 kpc), but their origin and persistence are unexplained—they resist mixing and thermal conduction in a collisional medium, and the standard mechanism (Field instability) is dismissed outside cores because conduction should suppress it.
AI.method: The authors propose that heat-flux-driven plasma instabilities anomalously suppress thermal conduction in weakly collisional/collisionless plasmas with local magnetic fields. They derive a new parameter regime for condensate formation overlapping with conditions outside cluster cores and use 1D hydrodynamic simulations to test their analytical predictions.
AI.result: Two key effects: (i) condensates can form in a parameter regime that overlaps with conditions outside the core, and (ii) condensates reach a steady state analogous to the hydrodynamic limit. This extends the instability-driven fluctuation regime to over ≥50% of the cluster (depending on hot plasma temperature).
AI.conclusion: The mechanism explains the origin and persistence of multiscale temperature fluctuations in the ICM outside cluster cores, significantly expanding the region where local thermal instability can operate.

title: Six decades of TIGRE and Mount Wilson chromospheric monitoring in the H and K lines: The quest for an understanding of solar-type activity
comment: accepted by A&A
summary: The combined time series of the consistently calibrated chromospheric activity indicator, the S-index -- derived from Mount Wilson and TIGRE data -- now spans more than five decades of monitoring observations of the Sun and of more than one hundred solar-like stars. For the first time, these data allow us to probe the long-term stability of solar-type magnetic cycles as well as their possible transition into other behavioral forms of stellar activity in the time domain. Such variability studies are an important input for solar-stellar connection research and for our empirical understanding of the long-term perspective of solar activity as well as of a wider empirical picture of the coevolution of magnetic activity with stellar structure. We here present and discuss a representative selection of cool main-sequence stars, for which such data are available. The excellent quality of our TIGRE data now more than doubles the number of known cyclic stars. Grading them (i.e., excellent, good, fair, and poor) and putting them into an evolutionary perspective, we find that stars more active than the Sun are also more likely to show cyclic variability than stars below solar activity. Furthermore, more active stars tend to have more regular cycles, while the solar mean S-value fits the lower end of the S-index range found for cyclic stars. This is consistent with the occurrence of solar Maunder minima episodes, hinting at a sometimes already unstable solar cycle. We find eighteen stars with even lower activity and lower variability than the Sun, which provide a preview into the latter's distant future.

AI.tldr: This paper uses over five decades of S-index data from Mount Wilson and TIGRE to analyze magnetic cycles in the Sun and over 100 solar-like stars, finding that more active stars show more regular cycles, while the Sun's activity sits at the lower end of cyclic stars, consistent with Maunder minima episodes, and identifies 18 stars with even lower activity that preview the Sun's distant future.
AI.motivation: To probe the long-term stability of solar-type magnetic cycles and transitions into other behavioral forms of stellar activity using five decades of consistently calibrated chromospheric activity data, enabling empirical understanding of the coevolution of magnetic activity with stellar structure.
AI.method: Combined time series of the S-index from Mount Wilson and TIGRE data spanning over 50 years for the Sun and more than 100 solar-like stars; stars were graded (excellent, good, fair, poor) and placed into an evolutionary perspective.
AI.result: TIGRE data more than doubles the number of known cyclic stars; stars more active than the Sun are more likely to show cyclic variability and more regular cycles; the solar mean S-value fits the lower end of the S-index range for cyclic stars; 18 stars found with lower activity and variability than the Sun.
AI.conclusion: The Sun's low cyclic activity is consistent with Maunder minima episodes indicating an already unstable solar cycle, and the identified lower-activity stars provide a preview of the Sun's distant future evolution.

title: Cluster vs Field: Clear Evidence for a Morphology-Density Relation in All Environments at $z\sim1.6$
comment: 23 pages, 13 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: We explore the relationship between galaxy structure, stellar mass, and local galaxy density in three SpARCS clusters at $z\sim1.6$ and compare with field galaxies from the 3D-HST survey. Our cluster and field data include: 1) unprecedented multiband photometry, allowing for accurate stellar mass estimates; 2) extensive slit and grism spectroscopy targeting both star-forming and quiescent galaxies, allowing for high-accuracy local density measurements; and 3) deep imaging in F160W, allowing for accurate rest-frame optical morphologies. Using Sérsic index measured in rest-frame R-band, we classify galaxies as disk-like, bulge-like, and intermediate. Our sample includes 111 cluster galaxies and 458 field galaxies with reliable Sérsic measurements. We find that a morphology-density relation is already in-place in both cluster and field galaxies at $z\sim1.6$, such that as local density increases, the fraction of bulge-like galaxies increases and disk-like galaxies decreases. Both samples show similar positive trends between median Sérsic index and local density. Additionally, we find a general positive relationship between Sérsic index and stellar mass. The majority of galaxies remain disk-like until reaching stellar masses above $10^{10.25} M_\odot$ in the cluster or $10^{10.8} M_\odot$ in the field, however, we cannot conclude whether the differences in stellar mass trends are significant. Overall, our results show clear morphology-density and morphology-mass relations in place at $z\sim1.6$ and oppose the idea that cluster-specific processes are solely responsible the morphology-density relation. Our data further suggest that the morphology-density relation may be independent of global environment at this epoch.

AI.tldr: Using SpARCS clusters and 3D-HST field galaxies at z~1.6, the authors find morphology-density and morphology-mass relations already in place, with bulge-like galaxies more common in denser regions and at higher stellar masses. The results suggest the morphology-density relation may be independent of global environment at this epoch, opposing cluster-specific processes as the sole driver.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the morphology-density relation (MDR) is already in place at z~1.6 and whether cluster-specific or environment-independent processes drive it, by comparing cluster and field galaxies at this early epoch.
AI.method: Analysis of Sérsic indices (rest-frame R-band) from deep F160W imaging for 111 cluster (SpARCS) and 458 field (3D-HST) galaxies at z~1.6, classified as disk-like, bulge-like, or intermediate, correlated with local galaxy density (from slit+grism spectroscopy) and stellar mass (from multiband photometry).
AI.result: MDR exists at z~1.6 in both cluster and field: bulge fraction increases and disk fraction decreases with local density. Positive Sérsic index–mass relation found. Most galaxies remain disk-like below ~10^10.25 M☉ (cluster) or ~10^10.8 M☉ (field). Trends are similar across environments, suggesting MDR may be independent of global environment.
AI.conclusion: Morphology-density and morphology-mass relations were already in place at z~1.6, and the data oppose cluster-specific processes as the sole origin of the MDR, instead favoring an environment-independent formation mechanism.

title: Constraints on Binarity for the Extreme Oe Variable Star AzV 493
comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to PASP
summary: The extreme Oe star AzV 493 is known to show unusual photometric and spectroscopic variability that suggest the presence of an unseen companion in a highly eccentric and long-period (7.3 or 14.6-year) orbit. We obtained a Chandra/ACIS observation near the putative periastron for the 7.3-year orbit to test for transient X-ray emission that would confirm its binary nature. Our data only place an upper limit to the X-ray luminosity of L_X < 2.5 x 10^33 erg/s based on the 0.5 - 8 keV flux limit. Additionally, we obtained 4 new spectroscopic observations with the M2FS spectrograph at Magellan and 20 archive FLAMES/GIRAFFE and X-Shooter spectra from ESO/VLT to further constrain the possibility of radial velocity (RV) variation. Statistical analysis of the RV measurements yields inconclusive results regarding the existence of variations. We discuss possible mass limits for a potential companion, which may be a black hole, in the event that the variations are real. The violet-to-red (V/R) Balmer ratio has also recently inverted, which may be a further indication of a companion.

AI.tldr: Using Chandra X-ray and optical spectroscopy, the study of AzV 493 found no X-ray emission (L_X < 2.5×10³³ erg/s) and inconclusive radial velocity variations, making the binary nature unconfirmed. Possible companion could be a black hole if variations are real.
AI.motivation: To test whether the extreme Oe star AzV 493 is a binary system with a compact companion (possibly a black hole) by searching for transient X-ray emission and constraining radial velocity variations near the predicted periastron of its proposed 7.3-year orbit.
AI.method: Chandra/ACIS X-ray observation near predicted periastron; 4 new M2FS/Magellan spectra + 20 archival FLAMES/GIRAFFE and X-Shooter/VLT spectra; statistical analysis of radial velocity measurements; V/R Balmer ratio monitoring.
AI.result: X-ray luminosity upper limit L_X < 2.5×10³³ erg/s (0.5-8 keV). Radial velocity variation analysis inconclusive. The V/R Balmer ratio has recently inverted.
AI.conclusion: Binary nature of AzV 493 remains unconfirmed; X-ray non-detection does not rule out a companion; if RV variations are real, a black hole companion is possible but not proven. The V/R Balmer inversion may hint at a companion but requires further investigation.

title: Quantifying the inside-out formation of disk galaxies at $1.5 \le z \le 3.0$
comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We examine the properties of galaxies at $1.5\le z\le3.0$ in the Extended Groth Strip (EGS) field to explore inside-out disk growth. We take advantage of the high-resolution James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) imaging and imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) to measure rest-frame optical and rest-frame UV half-light radii of the galaxies at comparable spatial resolution. We also examine the relation between structural properties and star formation rates, mass, and dust attenuation. While previous studies have inferred inside-out disk formation via the comparison of rest-optical and rest-UV radii using HST images, this study advances this knowledge by using the unprecedented resolution of JWST. We find evidence of inside-out disk formation from, on average, larger UV sizes than optical for galaxies across all redshifts. While previous studies suggested that this could be accounted for due to dust, we find that measurements with the improved resolution of the JWST support this size difference, after accounting for dust attenuation. We also observe that majority of galaxies with clumpy morphologies ($n < 0.5$) exhibit larger UV sizes than rest-optical because the star formation is distributed in multiple star forming clumps or mergers. We observe correlations in both the optical and UV for the size-mass relation, which are consistent with previous results but we find lower values for the slope of the power-law relation of the rest-optical fit, based on robust measurements from JWST images compared to the low resolution HST images used in previous studies.

AI.tldr: This study uses JWST and HST imaging to analyze galaxies at z=1.5-3.0 in the EGS field, finding evidence for inside-out disk growth based on larger UV half-light radii compared to optical, after accounting for dust attenuation. The improved resolution of JWST provides more robust measurements of structural properties and size-mass relations.
AI.motivation: To investigate inside-out disk growth in high-redshift galaxies (z=1.5-3.0) by leveraging the superior resolution of JWST to measure rest-frame optical and UV half-light radii, improving upon previous HST-based studies that were limited by lower spatial resolution and dust degeneracies.
AI.method: Analyzed galaxies in the Extended Groth Strip (EGS) at 1.5≤z≤3.0 using high-resolution JWST and HST imaging. Measured rest-frame optical and UV half-light radii at comparable spatial resolution, and examined relations between structural properties, star formation rates, mass, and dust attenuation.
AI.result: Found evidence for inside-out disk formation with larger UV than optical sizes across all redshifts, persisting after accounting for dust attenuation. Clumpy morphology galaxies (n<0.5) show larger UV sizes due to distributed star formation clumps/mergers. Size-mass relations show correlations consistent with previous studies but lower power-law slopes for rest-optical fits due to JWST's superior resolution.
AI.conclusion: JWST's improved resolution confirms inside-out disk growth at z=1.5-3.0, with the UV-optical size difference being intrinsic rather than solely dust-driven, and provides more accurate structural parameter measurements than earlier HST studies.

title: DKIST Unveils Four-Lobed Stokes U Profiles in a Magnetically Complex Sunspot Penumbra
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present DKIST spectropolarimetric observations of a sunspot penumbra revealing spatially coherent four-lobed Stokes U profiles that persist after polarimetric crosstalk correction. The observed Stokes vectors are well reproduced by stratified inversions containing gradients in velocity and magnetic parameters, including line-of-sight variation of the magnetic azimuth. Forward synthesis experiments in which the magnetic azimuth is artificially held constant with optical depth substantially modify the Stokes U morphology while leaving Stokes I, Q, and V comparatively unchanged, indicating that azimuthal variation is an important contributor to the observed linear polarisation signatures within the tested one-component atmospheres. We explored degeneracies using both two-component atmospheres and one-component constant-azimuth models: the former generally converged toward pathological solutions, while the latter provided a plausible degenerate explanation for much of the observed four-lobed Stokes U morphology. A supervised machine-learning classifier applied to Stokes V profiles shows that the associated magnetic complexity is spatially confined to the penumbra-light-bridge boundary where the four-lobed Stokes U profiles and reverse-polarity fields are observed. These results identify four-lobed Stokes U profiles as a potential spectropolarimetric signature of complex line-of-sight magnetic structuring in sunspot penumbrae, providing new observational constraints on fine-scale penumbral magnetic topology.

AI.tldr: DKIST observations of sunspot penumbrae reveal four-lobed Stokes U profiles caused by line-of-sight variations in magnetic azimuth, indicating complex magnetic structuring at penumbra-light-bridge boundaries.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of four-lobed Stokes U profiles in sunspot penumbrae and determine whether they arise from magnetic azimuth gradients along the line of sight, providing new observational constraints on fine-scale penumbral magnetic topology.
AI.method: DKIST spectropolarimetric observations with polarimetric crosstalk correction; stratified inversions with velocity and magnetic parameter gradients; forward synthesis experiments with constant azimuth; two-component and one-component constant-azimuth model comparison; supervised machine-learning classifier applied to Stokes V profiles.
AI.result: Four-lobed Stokes U profiles are spatially coherent and persist after crosstalk correction. Forward synthesis shows azimuthal variation significantly alters Stokes U while leaving I, Q, V largely unchanged. Two-component models converge to pathological solutions, while constant-azimuth models provide a plausible degenerate explanation. ML classifier shows magnetic complexity is confined to the penumbra-light-bridge boundary where reverse-polarity fields are observed.
AI.conclusion: Four-lobed Stokes U profiles are a spectropolarimetric signature of complex line-of-sight magnetic structuring in sunspot penumbrae, providing new observational constraints on fine-scale penumbral magnetic topology.

title: The 10-15 GHz radio continuum survey of the Galactic Plane with SKAO
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:26.06.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Traficante01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: Star formation emerges from the complex interplay between gravity, turbulence, magnetic fields, and stellar feedback, all of which vary across spatial scales and Galactic environments. Over the past decades, extensive multiwavelength surveys of the Galactic Plane have progressively unveiled this complexity. Far-infrared and sub-millimetre surveys have identified and characterized tens of thousands of star-forming regions, revealing their mass, temperature, and evolutionary stage. Complementary molecular-line surveys, spanning several CO transitions and isotopologues, have mapped the gas kinematics from giant molecular clouds down to sub-parsec structures. The advent of interferometers such as ALMA has revolutionized this field, enabling systematic studies of gas dynamics, fragmentation, and collapse in dense clumps at scales of a few thousand astronomical units. At the same time, mid-infrared and radio surveys at frequencies 0.8 <= nu <= 5 GHz have traced ionised gas associated with the earliest and latest phases of massive-star evolution, including thermal radio jets, hypercompact and ultracompact HII regions, supernova remnants, planetary nebulae, and evolved massive stars. Yet, a uniform, Galaxy-wide census of ionised structures and feedback processes remains elusive. A transformational leap forward requires a sensitive, high-resolution radio survey of the Galactic Plane at 10-15 GHz, capable of resolving physical scales smaller than 0.05 pc at distances up to 20 kpc. This is precisely the goal of the SKA-Mid Galactic Plane survey, which will, with its unprecedented sensitivity, angular resolution, and mapping speed, provide the first panoptic view of ionised gas and stellar feedback across the Milky Way.

AI.tldr: The paper reviews multiwavelength studies of star formation in the Galactic Plane, highlighting the complexity of gravity, turbulence, magnetic fields, and feedback across scales. It notes that while far-infrared, sub-millimetre, molecular-line, and interferometric surveys have advanced understanding, a uniform census of ionised gas and feedback is missing. The SKA-Mid Galactic Plane survey at 10-15 GHz will fill this gap with high sensitivity/resolution, providing a panoptic view of ionised gas and stellar feedback across the Milky Way.
AI.motivation: To emphasize the need for a Galaxy-wide, uniform census of ionised structures and stellar feedback processes, which remains elusive despite extensive multiwavelength surveys of star formation.
AI.method: Review of existing far-infrared, sub-millimetre, molecular-line, mid-infrared, and radio surveys (0.8–5 GHz), plus interferometric studies (e.g., ALMA), and proposal of the SKA-Mid Galactic Plane survey at 10–15 GHz with high sensitivity, angular resolution, and mapping speed to resolve scales <0.05 pc up to 20 kpc.
AI.result: Existing surveys have characterized star-forming regions, gas kinematics, fragmentation, and ionised gas from massive-star evolution, but lacked a uniform Galaxy-wide census of ionised structures and feedback. The SKA-Mid survey is identified as the transformational solution.
AI.conclusion: A sensitive, high-resolution radio survey at 10–15 GHz (SKA-Mid) is required to provide the first panoptic view of ionised gas and stellar feedback across the Milky Way, representing a transformational leap forward.

title: A Spitzer Space Telescope Exploration Science Program to Search for Y Dwarf Variability
comment: Accepted for publication in the Astronomical Journal
summary: We present the results of a Spitzer Space Telescope Exploration Science Program to search for and characterize variability in Y dwarfs. We observed 14 Y dwarfs over a 24 hr period at [3.6] and [4.5] and then repeated the observations a few months later. We add two Y dwarfs, WD 0806-661B and WISE J085510.83-071442.5, that were also observed with Spitzer so that our sample includes all Y dwarfs observed for variability with Spitzer. We infer variability fractions of 59%+-15% and 64%+10%-13% for [3.6], and [4.5], in the first epoch, and 35%+17% -11% and 75%+8% -15% in the second epoch. We also find that Y dwarf Spitzer light curves are generally stable over timescales of months, but in some cases can show clear changes in amplitude. Combining our results with a similar Spitzer survey of L and T dwarfs by Metchev et al. (2015), we find the mid-infrared variability fraction of L, T, and Y dwarfs weakly supports the hypothesis that brown dwarf variability is caused by variations in the horizontal and/or vertical structure of condensate clouds.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a Spitzer Space Telescope survey of 14 Y dwarfs (plus two additional sources) observed for mid-infrared variability at [3.6] and [4.5] over two epochs. Variability fractions range from 35% to 75% depending on band and epoch. Y dwarf light curves are generally stable over months but can show amplitude changes. Combined with L/T dwarf surveys, results weakly support condensate cloud variations as the cause of brown dwarf variability.
AI.motivation: To search for and characterize photometric variability in Y dwarfs using Spitzer Space Telescope, extending variability studies to the coldest brown dwarfs to understand the physical mechanisms driving atmospheric variability.
AI.method: Spitzer Exploration Science Program observing 14 Y dwarfs over 24 hr at [3.6] and [4.5], repeated months later, plus two additional Y dwarfs (WD 0806-661B and WISE J085510.83-071442.5). Variability fractions inferred from light curve analysis across two epochs.
AI.result: First epoch variability fractions: 59%±15% at [3.6], 64%+10%−13% at [4.5]. Second epoch: 35%+17%−11% at [3.6], 75%+8%−15% at [4.5]. Light curves are generally stable over months but some show amplitude changes. Combined with Metchev et al. (2015) L/T dwarf data, the mid-infrared variability fraction weakly supports condensate cloud variations as the cause.
AI.conclusion: Y dwarfs exhibit significant mid-infrared variability, with fractions varying by epoch and band. The variability is likely driven by horizontal and/or vertical structure changes in condensate clouds, though the support for this hypothesis is weak when combined with L and T dwarf results.

title: Wind Acceleration as a Driver of Detached Blueshifted Absorption in Quasar Disk Winds
comment: 1 Table, 4 Figures
summary: Active galactic nuclei (AGN) unification models often emphasize the viewing angle, $i$, but $i$ alone does not determine quasar properties. This is crucial for quasar outflows: UV absorption in Extremely High Velocity Outflow (EHVO) quasars can reach blueshifted velocities of $\sim0.2~c$. In disk-wind models, both $i$ and internal wind structure shape the emergent spectrum. We test their interplay using biconical quasar disk-wind models with different acceleration lengths, $R_v$, and generate synthetic spectra over a range of $i$. We use Monte Carlo radiative transfer to account for finite continuum sources, wind attenuation, scattering, reprocessing, and emission. Changing $R_v$ greatly alters the ionization structure, continuum shape, and absorption-line profiles. At intermediate viewing angles, sightlines pass through the fastest wind. Even there, highly detached and blueshifted \CIV\ absorption like that observed in EHVO quasars appears only in models with small $R_v$. In these models, the gas reaches high velocity before attaining the ionization and density conditions favorable for \CIV. Models with larger $R_v$ instead produce broader, less detached troughs, even when the terminal velocity is very high. Thus, highly detached and blueshifted absorption requires both a high terminal velocity and small $R_v$, making such features diagnostics of disk-wind acceleration and structure. EHVO quasars provide a clear example, but the same principle applies more broadly to highly detached and blueshifted absorption in quasar outflows. Our results support an extended disk-wind view of AGN unification: $i$ selects the observed wind region, while $R_v$ shapes the emergent spectrum and absorption morphology.

AI.tldr: The paper uses biconical disk-wind models with varying acceleration lengths (Rv) and viewing angles (i) to show that highly detached, blueshifted CIV absorption (like in EHVO quasars) requires both high terminal velocity and small Rv, demonstrating that AGN unification depends not only on viewing angle but also on internal wind structure.
AI.motivation: Standard AGN unification models emphasize viewing angle (i) alone, but this is insufficient to explain diverse quasar outflow properties such as the extremely high velocity outflows (EHVO) seen in some quasars.
AI.method: Biconical quasar disk-wind models with varying acceleration lengths (Rv) are constructed, and Monte Carlo radiative transfer is used to generate synthetic spectra across a range of viewing angles, accounting for finite continuum sources, wind attenuation, scattering, reprocessing, and emission.
AI.result: Small Rv models produce highly detached, blueshifted CIV absorption resembling EHVO quasars at intermediate viewing angles, while large Rv models yield broader, less detached troughs even at high terminal velocities. Changing Rv significantly alters ionization structure, continuum shape, and absorption-line profiles.
AI.conclusion: Highly detached blueshifted absorption requires both high terminal velocity and small Rv, making these features diagnostics of disk-wind acceleration. The results support an extended disk-wind AGN unification where i selects the observed wind region and Rv shapes the spectrum and absorption morphology.

title: Nautilus: Fast Time-Resolved Spectroscopy of GKM Stellar Flares and Their Implications for Planetary Habitability
comment: 9 pages, 1 figure, 1 table
summary: Low-mass GKM dwarfs are prime targets for finding habitable-zone Earth-sized planets, but their frequent flares, especially on M~dwarfs, can strongly affect planetary atmospheres through enhanced UV/XUV radiation and stellar proton events, which can drive complex photochemistry and accelerate atmospheric escape. Current atmospheric and habitability models of planets around low-mass stars often rely on simplified flare inputs, such as fixed-temperature blackbodies or approximate optical-to-UV/XUV conversions. However, recent observations show that M~dwarfs' flare temperatures and spectral shapes can vary significantly with flare energy, phase, and stellar type, and that optical-based flare observations may underestimate the flare energy in the UV. Time-resolved spectroscopic flare observations of G- and K-dwarfs also remain rare compared to those of M dwarfs. Here, we propose that the Nautilus Space Observatory concept can provide a unique opportunity to obtain fast-cadence, precisely flux-calibrated, moderate-resolution NUV-to-NIR spectroscopy of flares across a large sample of GKM dwarfs. These observations will measure the time-dependent flare energy budget from the near-UV/blue continuum to the optical and near-infrared continuum, while resolving key chromospheric lines that trace the underlying flare physics. We aim to construct a statistical library of empirical flare spectral templates organized by flare and stellar properties, including flare energy, flare phase, and host-star spectral type. This library will provide a practical bridge between observed stellar flare properties and the radiation inputs required for planetary atmospheric evolution and habitability simulations.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using the Nautilus Space Observatory to obtain fast-cadence, flux-calibrated NUV-to-NIR spectroscopy of flares across GKM dwarfs, aiming to build a statistical library of empirical flare spectral templates to improve inputs for planetary atmospheric and habitability models.
AI.motivation: Current atmospheric and habitability models for planets around low-mass stars rely on oversimplified flare inputs (fixed-temperature blackbodies or approximate UV/XUV conversions), while observations show flare temperatures and spectral shapes vary significantly with energy, phase, and stellar type, and optical observations may underestimate UV flare energy.
AI.method: The Nautilus Space Observatory concept will perform fast-cadence, precisely flux-calibrated, moderate-resolution NUV-to-NIR spectroscopy of flares across a large sample of GKM dwarfs, measuring time-dependent flare energy budgets from NUV/blue to optical/NIR continuum and resolving key chromospheric lines.
AI.result: A statistical library of empirical flare spectral templates organized by flare energy, flare phase, and host-star spectral type will be constructed.
AI.conclusion: This empirical library will provide a practical bridge between observed stellar flare properties and the radiation inputs needed for planetary atmospheric evolution and habitability simulations.

title: Probing the molecular gas content of galaxies in an over-dense group at z~0.7: a test case for environmental quenching
comment: 15 pages, 14 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: To probe the impact of group environment on molecular gas reservoirs at intermediate redshift, we observed the CO(2-1) emission in the galaxy group COSMOS-Gr30 at $z \sim 0.7$ with IRAM's NOEMA and 30m telescopes. This dense environment, located at the intersection of large-scale cosmic web filaments, has the specificity to host a large ($\sim 10^{4}$ kpc$^{2}$) ionized gas structure revealed by MUSE. We detect CO emission in four galaxies of the group at $\mathrm{S/N} > 5$ and derive upper limits for the remaining group members with secure spectroscopic redshifts. Stacked measurements indicate that group galaxies exhibit on average molecular gas contents reduced by $\sim 0.5$ dex relative to field scaling relations, corresponding to gas fractions that are $20\%$ to $40\%$ of those found in typical main-sequence galaxies. Although the uncertainties are significant, this suggests that environmental processes efficiently deplete molecular gas reservoirs in the galaxies of this group. The 30m observations place an upper limit on the molecular gas associated with the extended ionized structure, $M_{\rm gas} < 2 \times 10^{10} \rm M_\odot$, implying that less than a third of the gas in the intra-group medium is in a cold, star-forming phase. Together, these results contribute to show how environmental mechanisms in dense group environments act to remove or suppress molecular gas within galaxies, capturing quenching processes in action.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the molecular gas content in the galaxy group COSMOS-Gr30 at z~0.7 using NOEMA and 30m CO(2-1) observations. Group galaxies show ~0.5 dex reduced molecular gas compared to field scaling relations, with gas fractions only 20-40% of typical main-sequence galaxies. An upper limit on cold gas in the extended ionized intra-group medium is derived, indicating that environmental processes are actively depleting molecular gas in this dense group environment.
AI.motivation: To understand how group environments impact molecular gas reservoirs in galaxies at intermediate redshift, specifically probing environmental quenching mechanisms in a dense group located at the intersection of cosmic web filaments, which also hosts a large ionized gas structure revealed by MUSE.
AI.method: NOEMA and IRAM 30m observations of CO(2-1) emission in the COSMOS-Gr30 group at z~0.7. CO detection in 4 group members (S/N>5), upper limits for other secure spectroscopic members, and stacked measurements to compare with field scaling relations. Additionally, 30m observations to constrain molecular gas in the extended ionized intra-group medium.
AI.result: Group galaxies show ~0.5 dex reduced molecular gas content relative to field scaling relations, with gas fractions 20-40% of typical main-sequence galaxies. Upper limit on molecular gas in extended ionized structure: M_gas < 2×10^10 M_sun, implying <1/3 of intra-group medium gas is in a cold, star-forming phase.
AI.conclusion: Environmental processes efficiently deplete molecular gas reservoirs in dense group environments, capturing quenching processes in action. The results demonstrate how group mechanisms remove or suppress molecular gas within galaxies, with the intra-group medium being predominantly in a warm ionized phase rather than cold molecular phase.

title: Dust Formation in Common Envelope Binary Interactions -- III. Lightcurves
comment: 23 pages, 18 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: Luminous red novae are transient events thought to arise from common envelope binary interactions. In this paper, we perform post-processing light-curve calculations for two, 3D hydrodynamic simulations of common envelope events. These simulations model interactions between 1.7 $M_\odot$ and 3.7 $M_\odot$ asymptotic giant branch stars and a 0.6 $M_\odot$ compact companion, including dust nucleation. In both our simulations, which are carried out for 44 years under adiabatic conditions, we observe a bright, hot peak lasting $3-5$ years, primarily due to the expansion of the photosphere before and during inspiral. Additional peaks can be seen appearing at different times and for different viewing angles, due to the asymmetry of the interaction. Dust forms about $1-3$ years after the beginning of the simulated interaction and shortly afterwards we witness a sharp decline in the bolometric luminosity, followed by a partial recovery and a plateau with an effective temperature of $\sim$400 K. The dust photosphere reaches a size of $\sim$250 au by the end of the simulations, but we predict that between 100 and 200 years, the dust will become optically thin at visible wavelengths, revealing an inner, warmer photosphere. The lightcurves obtained have two, well-quantified, but large uncertainties: insufficient surface resolution primarily affecting the first 1-2 years of the simulated lightcurves and the adiabatic assumption that affects primarily the later years. We finally contextualise our simulations within a group of observed luminous red nova transients, drawing particular attention to the outburst of OGLE-2002-BLG-360 and AT 2025abao, which are the closest match to our simulation.

AI.tldr: The paper presents post-processing light-curve calculations from two 3D simulations of common envelope binary interactions between AGB stars and compact companions. The simulations show a bright hot peak lasting 3-5 years from photosphere expansion, dust formation after 1-3 years causing a luminosity decline followed by a plateau at ~400 K, and predicted dust dispersal after 100-200 years. The lightcurves best match observed luminous red novae OGLE-2002-BLG-360 and AT 2025abao.
AI.motivation: Luminous red novae are transient events thought to arise from common envelope binary interactions, and this work aims to connect 3D hydrodynamic simulations of these events to observable light curves.
AI.method: The authors performed post-processing light-curve calculations for two 3D hydrodynamic simulations of common envelope events (1.7 M☉ and 3.7 M☉ AGB stars with 0.6 M☉ compact companions), run for 44 years under adiabatic conditions including dust nucleation. Lightcurves were computed for different viewing angles, with quantified uncertainties from surface resolution and adiabatic assumption.
AI.result: Simulations show a bright hot peak (3-5 years) from photosphere expansion, additional asymmetric peaks at different viewing angles, dust formation 1-3 years post-interaction causing a sharp bolometric luminosity decline, followed by partial recovery and a ~400 K plateau. The dust photosphere reaches ~250 au by the end, predicted to become optically thin in 100-200 years. Best matches are OGLE-2002-BLG-360 and AT 2025abao.
AI.conclusion: The simulated lightcurves reproduce key features of observed luminous red novae, with two main uncertainties: insufficient surface resolution (affecting first 1-2 years) and adiabatic assumption (affecting later years). The closest observed counterparts are OGLE-2002-BLG-360 and AT 2025abao.

title: Probing the Nature of Lyman Continuum Emitting and Low-metallicity Galaxies Using the SKA
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKAII (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Bait01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary:
The sources responsible for cosmic reionization remain a key open question in observational cosmology. Recent JWST results increasingly suggest that low-mass star-forming galaxies (e.g., compact starbursts and strong emission-line systems) dominated the ionizing photon budget. The physical mechanisms driving Lyman continuum (LyC) photon escape, including supernova, radiative, and cosmic-ray feedback, and the origin of extreme ionization conditions, remain poorly understood. Radio continuum (RC) emission, a well-established star-formation tracer in normal galaxies, is not yet well characterized in such extreme systems, which exhibit high star-formation rate densities, young stellar populations, low metallicity, and hard ionizing spectra.
  Targeted mid-frequency ($1-15$,GHz) observations with SKA precursors have begun probing low-redshift LyC emitters (LCEs), revealing links between RC spectral index, LyC escape fraction, ionization conditions, metallicity, and SFR surface density, alongwith deviations from the canonical RC$-$SFR relation. The higher sensitivity of the SKA Array Assemblies across Bands $\sim 1-5$ will enable systematic studies of fainter LCEs and low-mass, metal-poor galaxies. We present number density predictions for LCE candidates at $z \sim 1$-$3$, showing that SKA-Mid surveys can assemble samples of $\sim10-100$ candidates per square degree over a star-formation rate range of $1-100$,$M_{\odot}$yr$^{-1}$, making a dedicated SKA Large Programme scientifically feasible.
  With the full SKA, in synergy with JWST and next generation telescopes, multi-wavelength analyses will robustly constrain the thermal and non-thermal RC components and cosmic-ray energy spectra, providing critical insights into the feedback processes governing LyC escape and star formation in the early universe.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses how SKA precursors and the full SKA, combined with JWST and next-generation telescopes, can systematically study low-mass star-forming galaxies that likely dominated cosmic reionization, by probing radio continuum emission from Lyman continuum emitters to understand feedback processes and LyC photon escape mechanisms.
AI.motivation: The sources responsible for cosmic reionization remain a key open question in observational cosmology, and the physical mechanisms driving LyC photon escape and extreme ionization conditions are poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors present number density predictions for LCE candidates at z~1-3 using SKA-Mid surveys, and propose multi-wavelength analyses combining SKA with JWST and next-generation telescopes to constrain thermal/non-thermal RC components and cosmic-ray energy spectra.
AI.result: SKA-Mid surveys can assemble samples of ~10-100 LCE candidates per square degree over an SFR range of 1-100 M⊙/yr, making a dedicated SKA Large Programme feasible.
AI.conclusion: With the full SKA and synergies with JWST and next-generation telescopes, multi-wavelength analyses will robustly constrain feedback processes governing LyC escape and star formation in the early universe.

title: Investigating the System Configuration of Kepler-451 through Orbital Period Variations: Dynamical and Magnetic Interpretations
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables, published in ApJ
summary: We present an analysis of eclipse timing variations in Kepler-451 using data spanning 2004-2024 from both ground- and space-based observations. Using two datasets, DS-A and DS-B, we constructed updated O-C diagrams. By modeling both datasets with various LTT configurations, we tested for the presence of circumbinary companions. For DS-A, the two-companion model (LTT34) provides the best fit with RMS = 3.23 s and chi^2_nu = 1.23, while inclusion a fifth body (LTT345) does not improve the fit (RMS = 3.24 s, chi^2_nu = 1.28). For DS-B, the three-companion model (LTT345) yields the best fit (RMS = 2.31 s, chi^2_nu = 1.01), although the semi-amplitude of the inner companion (1.34 s) is smaller than the systematic error (1.81 s), suggesting that it may originate from observational or calibration systematics. Applegate-mechanism tests indicate that most signals exceed the available energy budget, while the outer LTT terms in both datasets remain consistent with the Standard model and may have a magnetic origin. Removing these magnetic terms yields dynamically stable configurations for at least 10^7 yr. These findings support the presence of a second-generation circumbinary planet at 3.4 AU around Kepler-451, while the origin of the remaining LTT signals remains uncertain.

AI.tldr: Analysis of eclipse timing variations in Kepler-451 (2004-2024) reveals evidence for a second-generation circumbinary planet at ~3.4 AU, but other LTT signals may originate from magnetic activity or systematics rather than additional companions.
AI.motivation: To investigate the presence of circumbinary companions around the Kepler-451 system by analyzing eclipse timing variations over two decades using both ground- and space-based observations.
AI.method: Constructed O-C diagrams from two datasets (DS-A and DS-B); modeled with various LTT configurations (two-companion LTT34, three-companion LTT345); performed Applegate-mechanism tests to distinguish between dynamical and magnetic origins of timing signals.
AI.result: DS-A best fit: LTT34 (RMS=3.23 s, χ²_ν=1.23); LTT345 no improvement. DS-B best fit: LTT345 (RMS=2.31 s, χ²_ν=1.01) but inner companion amplitude (1.34 s) below systematic error (1.81 s). Outer LTT terms consistent with magnetic origin; removing magnetic terms yields stable configurations for ≥10⁷ yr.
AI.conclusion: Supports a second-generation circumbinary planet at ~3.4 AU around Kepler-451; origin of remaining LTT signals remains uncertain, possibly magnetic rather than planetary.

title: Columba: isolated dwarf galaxy populations in diverse cosmological environments simulated with a cold interstellar medium
comment: accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We introduce a suite of LambdaCDM cosmological, hydrodynamical simulations that track the evolution of a large population of dwarf galaxies. The suite comprises zoom-in simulations of 25 spherical, under-dense regions of r=5cMpc, selected to span $\approx1.5$ dex in mean enclosed density, covering voids to filamentary structures, whilst excluding haloes of Milky Way-mass or larger. The simulations achieve a mass resolution of $\sim 10^5$ solar masses with a galaxy formation model including cold, dense interstellar gas and whose subgrid stellar feedback efficiency reproduces the z=0 galaxy stellar mass function. We investigate the impact of the cosmic environment on dwarf galaxy formation and evolution. We find that the 5 cMpc environment influences the normalisation of the halo and galaxy mass functions, but does not significantly affect the stellar mass - halo mass (SMHM) relation and halo occupation fraction for galaxies with $M_{\star}=10^6-10^9$ solar masses. Instead, host halo concentration, estimated from DM-only counterparts, is more important: both the fraction of haloes hosting a resolved galaxy and the scatter about the SMHM relation correlate positively with concentration. Owing to halo assembly bias, concentration also influences galaxy formation times, such that at fixed halo mass more concentrated haloes host galaxies that are both older and more massive. The offset from the mean SMHM relation also anti-correlates with $t_{90}$, the time at which 90 percent of a galaxy's stellar mass has assembled. These correlations between halo properties and galaxy star formation histories present testable predictions for forthcoming observational surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper presents zoom-in cosmological simulations of 25 under-dense regions (voids to filaments) to study dwarf galaxy formation, finding that the large-scale environment influences mass function normalization but not the stellar mass-halo mass relation or occupation fraction; instead, halo concentration (linked to assembly bias) is the key driver of galaxy properties and star formation histories.
AI.motivation: To understand how cosmic environment (from voids to filaments) impacts dwarf galaxy formation and evolution, using high-resolution simulations that properly resolve dwarf galaxies.
AI.method: Zoom-in cosmological hydrodynamical simulations of 25 spherical under-dense regions (r=5 cMpc), spanning ~1.5 dex in mean enclosed density, with mass resolution ~10^5 solar masses and subgrid stellar feedback calibrated to match the z=0 stellar mass function.
AI.result: The 5 cMpc environment affects normalization of halo and galaxy mass functions but not the SMHM relation or halo occupation fraction for M* = 10^6-10^9 Msun. Host halo concentration is more important: it correlates positively with both occupation fraction and scatter about the SMHM relation. More concentrated haloes host older and more massive galaxies. Offset from mean SMHM anti-correlates with t90 (90% mass assembly time).
AI.conclusion: Halo concentration, driven by assembly bias, is the primary determinant of dwarf galaxy properties rather than the large-scale cosmic environment. The correlations between halo concentration and galaxy star formation histories provide testable predictions for observational surveys.

title: Chemical Complexity in the Early Stages of Star Formation in the SKAO Era
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Bianchi01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: About 350 molecules have been identified in the interstellar medium (ISM), including complex molecules relevant to prebiotic chemistry. A remarkable level of molecular diversity has been observed from the earliest stages of star formation, providing the initial chemical inventory inherited by planetary systems. Radio observations have played a pivotal role in these discoveries, starting with the identification of the first polyatomic molecule, $\text{NH}_3$ (Cheung et al. 1968). (Sub-)millimeter observations have revealed complex organic molecules of prebiotic relevance, including formamide ($\text{NH}_2\text{CHO}$), glycolaldehyde ($\text{CH}_2\text{OHCHO}$), and even urea ($(\text{NH}_2)_2\text{CO}$), and hydroxylamine ($\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$), which are possible precursors of RNA nucleotides (Ceccarelli et al. 2023; Jiménez-Serra et al. 2020). However, in dense protostellar regions, dust opacity hampers the detection of molecular emission. Additionally, large molecules and those containing heavy atoms, which have rotational transitions at lower frequencies, often remain inaccessible to current instruments. The Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) will provide an unprecedented combination of sensitivity and angular resolution at radio wavelengths. This will allow for the detection of prebiotic species and offer new insights into the chemical pathways that shape emerging planetary systems (Jiménez-Serra et al. 2022). This chapter details the scientific questions and advancements that the SKAO, and more specifically, SKA-Mid equipped with the Band 5 receivers, will pursue in the field of astrochemistry, focusing on the chemical complexity in both high-mass and solar-type star-forming regions.

AI.tldr: This chapter discusses how SKAO (SKA-Mid with Band 5 receivers) will enable detection of prebiotic complex organic molecules in star-forming regions, overcoming current limitations of dust opacity and frequency accessibility in radio astrochemistry.
AI.motivation: Current radio observations face limitations: dust opacity in dense protostellar regions blocks molecular emission, and large/heavy-atom molecules with low-frequency rotational transitions are inaccessible to existing instruments, hindering the study of prebiotic chemistry in star-forming environments.
AI.method: The SKAO, specifically SKA-Mid equipped with Band 5 receivers, will provide unprecedented sensitivity and angular resolution at radio wavelengths to detect molecular emission from prebiotic species in both high-mass and solar-type star-forming regions.
AI.result: The enhanced capabilities will enable the detection of prebiotic complex organic molecules (e.g., RNA nucleotide precursors) and reveal chemical pathways shaping emerging planetary systems, expanding beyond the ~350 molecules currently identified in the ISM.
AI.conclusion: SKA-Mid Band 5 will revolutionize astrochemistry by overcoming current observational barriers, allowing detailed study of chemical complexity and prebiotic molecular inventories inherited by planetary systems from the earliest stages of star formation.

title: UV Star-Formation Rates of the SHIELD Dwarf Galaxies
comment: 21 pages, 14 figures. Paper accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The Survey of HI in Extremely Low-mass Dwarfs (SHIELD) is a multi-wavelength observational project targeting gas-rich, star-forming dwarf galaxies at the faint end of the HI mass function. We present near-ultraviolet (NUV) and far-ultraviolet (FUV) flux measurements obtained from GALEX survey images and use these fluxes to derive FUV star-formation rates (SFRs) for all 75 SHIELD galaxies with GALEX data. This paper represents the first published analysis that makes use of the full SHIELD sample. We compare the FUV SFRs to a variety of physical quantities to better understand the nature of SHIELD galaxies. When comparing the H$α$ SFRs to the FUV SFRs for SHIELD and other local galaxy surveys, we confirm and solidify previous results that show that H$α$-based SFRs for dwarf galaxies can grossly underestimate the true rate of star formation, emphasizing the highly stochastic nature of star formation in extremely low-mass galaxies. We further show that FUV SFRs appear to be robust tracers of star formation down to the very lowest galaxy masses included in this study. We show that baryonic mass is the best mass-related tracer for the prediction of the FUV SFR of the galaxies in our sample. Not surprisingly, the SHIELD dwarf galaxies exhibit long gas-depletion timescales and large gas mass fractions: fully 68% of the SHIELD galaxies have gas masses that are larger than their stellar masses.

AI.tldr: The SHIELD project presents FUV and NUV flux measurements from GALEX for 75 low-mass dwarf galaxies, deriving FUV-based SFRs. The analysis confirms that Hα-based SFRs underestimate true star formation in dwarfs due to stochasticity, shows FUV SFRs are robust tracers even at the lowest masses, identifies baryonic mass as the best mass tracer for SFR prediction, and reveals that 68% of SHIELD galaxies have gas masses exceeding their stellar masses, implying long gas-depletion timescales.
AI.motivation: To understand star formation processes in extremely low-mass dwarf galaxies at the faint end of the HI mass function, which are poorly characterized due to their stochastic star formation and faintness, by leveraging multi-wavelength UV data from GALEX.
AI.method: NUV and FUV flux measurements were obtained from GALEX survey images for 75 SHIELD galaxies. These fluxes were used to derive FUV-based SFRs, which were then compared to Hα-based SFRs and other physical quantities across the full SHIELD sample and other local galaxy surveys.
AI.result: Hα-based SFRs systematically underestimate the true SFR in dwarf galaxies due to stochastic star formation. FUV SFRs are robust tracers down to the lowest galaxy masses. Baryonic mass is the best predictor of FUV SFR. 68% of SHIELD galaxies have gas masses larger than stellar masses, indicating long gas-depletion timescales.
AI.conclusion: FUV-based SFRs are a reliable star formation tracer for extremely low-mass dwarf galaxies, whereas Hα-based SFRs are unreliable in this regime. The gas-rich nature and long depletion timescales of SHIELD galaxies suggest they are in an early or slowly evolving phase of star formation.

title: MUSE Imaging Spectroscopy of the Fullerene Planetary Nebula Tc 1
comment: 24 pages, 5 Appendices, 11 tables and 17 figures (PDF). Accepted by A&A
summary:
The planetary nebula Tc 1 (PN G345.2 -08.8), one of the rare group of Galactic PNe showing fullerene emission in the infrared, was observed with MUSE wide field mode with adaptive optics, wavelength range 4750-9300A. Extinction, electron temperature (T_e) and density (N_e) images are presented from collisionally excited and recombination line ratios. The nebula has a high surface brightness 12 arcsec core, an elliptical ring of major axis 2.8 arcsec around the central star and some low ionization knots, and an extended halo 55 arcsec in size; between the core and halo is an annulus with intermediate properties, including higher T_e and lower N_e than in the core. The image of optical extinction from H Balmer line ratios is highly structured, and shows an annulus, adjacent to the core, of low extinction, lower than the line-of-sight interstellar extinction. Instrumental effects to account for this anomalously low extinction area are investigated and intrinsic effects from the scattering properties of nebular dust; neither can entirely explain the low-extinction region and the most likely cause is a local non-standard dust reddening law. This low extinction region also shows an anomalously high He I 7281/6678A line ratio, possibly caused by a contaminating line, but none were conclusively identified. The spectrum of the central star was extracted and fitted by a 31000K model atmosphere and is of type O7.5I(f). Over extended regions an enhancement of the detected continuum above the nebular continuum was found, as also seen in some other PNe observed with MUSE.
  The annulus of low extinction occurs outside the region of strongest fullerene emission, in the zone where N_e declines and T_e rises. A change in dust properties linked to conditions in this transition region between the higher density core nebula and lower density halo is deduced. (Abridged)

AI.tldr: MUSE observations of the planetary nebula Tc 1 reveal structured extinction, temperature, and density maps. A low-extinction annulus adjacent to the core cannot be fully explained by instrumental effects or standard dust scattering; a non-standard dust reddening law is proposed. This region coincides with a transition zone between the dense core and diffuse halo, where fullerene emission declines and electron temperature rises, suggesting a change in dust properties.
AI.motivation: To investigate the physical conditions, dust properties, and extinction structure of the fullerene-rich planetary nebula Tc 1 using integral-field optical spectroscopy, particularly to understand the anomalously low extinction region and its relation to fullerene emission.
AI.method: MUSE wide field mode with adaptive optics (4750-9300Å) was used to produce extinction, electron temperature (T_e), and electron density (N_e) maps from collisionally excited and recombination line ratios. The central star spectrum was extracted and fitted with a model atmosphere.
AI.result: Tc 1 shows a 12 arcsec high-surface-brightness core, a 2.8 arcsec elliptical ring around the central star, low-ionization knots, and a 55 arcsec halo. A low-extinction annulus adjacent to the core is found, lower than interstellar extinction, which cannot be fully explained by instrumental effects or scattering; a non-standard dust reddening law is likely. This region also shows an anomalously high He I 7281/6678Å ratio. The central star is O7.5I(f) type with T_eff~31000K. The low-extinction annulus lies outside the strongest fullerene emission zone, where N_e declines and T_e rises.
AI.conclusion: A change in dust properties occurs in the transition region between the dense core and the diffuse halo of Tc 1, linked to the physical conditions where fullerene emission fades and electron temperature increases.

title: Predicted Capabilities of the SPRITE SmallSat for a Low-Redshift Lyman Continuum Emission Survey
comment: Accepted for publication in the Journal of Astronomical Telescopes, Instruments, and Systems on June 22, 2026. 30 pages with 17 figures and 3 tables
